in_text_mentions: An 18-year-old female presented with primary amenorrhea. On examination, the patient's secondary sexual characteristics were found to be normal. An MRI of the pelvis was performed [Figures 1–3]. The sagittal T2 W MRI [Figure 1] demonstrated absence of uterus and upper vagina. The axial T2 FS images [Figures 2 and 3] confirmed the presence of normal ovaries with follicles and absence of vagina between the rectum and bladder. The visualized portions of the kidneys were unremarkable. No other abnormalities were identified.

panels.rationale: Single sagittal pelvic MRI from a case report titled for vaginal agenesis with uterine cervix atresia. The image is a real patient scan showing a malformed/unicornuate uterus distended with intraluminal blood (hematometra) and an adnexal horn, with the in-text explicitly attributing the MRI findings to vaginal aplasia and hematometra from obstructed outflow. This is a specific radiologic manifestation of the configured disease (vaginal agenesis), not a diagram, control, or other disease. The presentation (functional unicornuate uterus with cervical atresia causing hematometra rather than classic absent uterus) is a recognized less-common form, hence variant. No skin, ethnicity, or age is stated. [raw subtype: unicornuate uterus with cervical atresia]

A: Real-patient axial pelvic MRI (caption and in-text explicitly assign Figures 1(a) and 1(b) to MRI) from a disease-focused article on Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser (vaginal agenesis) syndrome. The image shows the pelvic/Müllerian anatomy of a confirmed MRKH patient with a complex right adnexal mass (leiomyoma) and a retroverted uterus; the mass is interpreted as arising from a rudimentary Müllerian remnant, which is an MRI correlate of the underlying Müllerian anomaly. Presentation is explicitly a rare case (atypical). No vocabulary key for absent uterus fits because the uterus is described as present/retroverted, and no vaginal assessment is given, so confidence is moderate. B: Second axial MRI slice of the same confirmed MRKH (vaginal agenesis) patient, showing the same complex right adnexal/pelvic mass and pelvic Müllerian anatomy; attributed to vaginal agenesis via the disease-focused article title together with the captioned MRI...
